title: Resolving the extended atmosphere and the inner wind of Mira (o Ceti) with long ALMA baselines
question: What are the physical conditions (density, temperature, SiO/H2O abundance, infall/outflow velocities) in Mira's extended atmosphere and inner wind, as probed by long-baseline ALMA continuum and SiO/H2O lines, and how do hydrodynamical models compare?

data.bands: Band 3 and Band 6 observed; Band 6 (229 GHz) lines analysed

what.value: CODEX o54 model atmosphere structures (density, temperature, velocity) provided by developers

evidence.quote: From the CODEX developers we have obtained the atmospheric structure information of the `o54` model series

external_data.citation: Ireland et al. 2008, 2011; Scholz et al. 2014 (cite: ireland2008; ireland2011; scholz2014)

what.value: SiO-He collisional rate coefficients (scaled by 1.38 for H2)

evidence.quote: extrapolated from the scaled (by 1.38) rate coefficients between SiO–He collisions as derived by (cite: dayou2006)
we adopt the value of $R_{\star}$ to be $12.3\,{\rm mas}$ (or $292\,R_{\astrosun}$) as determined by (cite: perrin2004)

recipe.goal: Image continuum and fit continuum visibilities
recipe.method: Fit uniform disk / Gaussian models to Band 6 continuum visibilities for Mira A and B

recipe.goal: Image SiO and H2O line cubes and extract spectra
recipe.method: clean without continuum subtraction; spectra extracted at centre and at radii 32-160 mas along PA 0, 90, 180, 270 deg

recipe.goal: Radiative transfer modelling of SiO and H2O spectra
recipe.method: 1-D RATRAN Monte Carlo models with power-law density/temperature, SiO two-step abundance, pseudo-continuum core, mixed infall/outflow velocity (Model 3); models convolved with the clean beam and compared by eye
key_parameters: SiO abundance drop at r_cond = 1.0e14 cm (~5 R*), outer ~1% of inner; H2O abundance 5.0e-6 (5.0e-5 near photosphere)
assumptions: Collisional partner purely rotational ground-state H2; spherical symmetry; distance 110 pc; R* = 12.3 mas

recipe.method: Use CODEX o54 density (scaled by 1e4), temperature and velocity as RATRAN inputs; modify radio-continuum radius to hide strong shocks
assumptions: m_part = 0.7 m_H2 + 0.3 m_He, helium mass fraction 0.3

answer_key.quantity: Mira A radio photosphere brightness temperature (uniform disk)

evidence.quote: The brightness temperature of the uniform disk model of Mira A is found to be $2611 \pm 51\,{\rm K}$.

answer_key.quantity: Mira A total continuum flux at 229.6 GHz

evidence.quote: the total flux of Mira A is $149.70 \pm 0.04\,{\rm mJy}$ and that of Mira B is $11.19 \pm 0.04\,{\rm mJy}$
we derive an independent spectral index (using the spectral line windows in Band 6 only) of $1.82 \pm 0.33$
with the shock velocity of $\Delta V \lesssim 12\,\ensuremath{\,{\rm km}\,{\rm s}^{-1}}$, near the radio photosphere of Mira

answer_key.quantity: SiO depletion radius and gas temperature

evidence.quote: gas-phase SiO starts to deplete at a radius of *at least* $4\,R_{\star}$ and a gas temperature of ${\lesssim}600\,{\rm K}$

answer_key.quantity: Gas density just beyond radio photosphere

evidence.quote: The gas density reaches $10^{12}$–$10^{13}\,{\rm cm}^{-3}$ just beyond the radio photosphere.

The infall velocity immediately above this expanding layer is about $7.3\,\ensuremath{\,{\rm km}\,{\rm s}^{-1}}$, and the expansion velocity below this layer is about $4.0\,\ensuremath{\,{\rm km}\,{\rm s}^{-1}}$.

not_stated_but_needed: Exact line-free channel ranges used in uvcontsub (only said to differ from CASA Guide script)
Exact clean parameters (niter, masks, spw/channel regridding) and which self-cal tables
Full numerical RATRAN input profiles (density, T, velocity, abundance power-law indices) for Model 3
RATRAN grid, photon count and convergence settings
Formal fitting/goodness-of-fit method for the models (fit by eye, no stated metric)
CODEX file contents are private (provided by developers)
score_reason: Public SV data and detailed imaging settings, but modelling is empirical with unpublished input profiles and no fit statistics.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, continuum fits and imaging recipe are numeric and redoable; the radiative transfer part is only partly reproducible.
